UserGuide.studentCourse.title: Course page
UserGuide.studentHome.title: Home
UserGuide.studentHome.step1.title: Start with your ongoing courses
UserGuide.studentHome.step1.text: Courses appear here for their entire duration, not just on class day. Green means the class is currently in session; you can still click into other courses to use machines, check assignments, or practice after class.
UserGuide.studentHome.step2.title: Quick practice doesn't need manual review
UserGuide.studentHome.step2.text: When you need to quickly test a command or do some lightweight practice, choose a template and fill in a container name and password — the system approves it automatically and starts creating it.
UserGuide.studentHome.step3.title: After-class practice or independent research
UserGuide.studentHome.step3.text: When it's not time for class, you can pick up where you left off in your last course from here; independent research takes you to a resource request instead.
UserGuide.studentHome.step4.title: This is the class you're taking right now
UserGuide.studentHome.step4.text: The course name, class time, and "In session" status are all shown on this card. Check here first on the home page to know which class to join today.
UserGuide.studentHome.step5.title: This is your chapter completion progress
UserGuide.studentHome.step5.text: The progress bar shows how much of the current chapter you've completed — it is not the machine creation progress. This number moves forward as you finish tasks.
UserGuide.studentHome.step6.title: Click directly on the classroom machine you want to use
UserGuide.studentHome.step6.text: Machines assigned by your teacher are listed directly here. Click anywhere on a machine card to start and enter it; the info button on the right takes you to "My Resources" to view full settings.
UserGuide.studentHome.step7.title: Check whether the environment is ready first
UserGuide.studentHome.step7.text: "Environment ready" means you can get started. The IP is the connection address; "Usable until" is when this classroom machine expires.
UserGuide.studentHome.step8.title: Check completion counts here
UserGuide.studentHome.step8.text: Each task has its own completion checkbox. Tick it when you're done, and untick it any time if it isn't finished yet.
UserGuide.studentHome.step9.title: These are the grading items your teacher has assigned to AI
UserGuide.studentHome.step9.text: Only checks your teacher has approved are shown here. This only records your completion status; it doesn't start an AI check or judge whether you're right or wrong.
UserGuide.myRequests.title: My Requests
UserGuide.myRequests.step1.title: Only apply here for independent research
UserGuide.myRequests.step1.text: When you need to set up your own project or research machine, click "Request Resource" and fill in your requirements. Classroom machines assigned by your teacher don't need to be requested again.
UserGuide.myRequests.step2.title: The status shows what stage the request is at
UserGuide.myRequests.step2.text: "Under review" means it's waiting for your teacher to process; "Provisioned" means the machine has been created; "Provisioning failed" lets you click retry. Click a row to expand the request reason and detailed timestamps.
UserGuide.myResources.title: My Resources
UserGuide.myResources.step1.title: These numbers are your usage quota
UserGuide.myResources.step1.text: The number on the left is your current usage; the one on the right is your available limit. For example, "2 / 4 units" means you've used 2 and can have up to 4. When you're close to the limit, you'll need to release a resource first.
UserGuide.myResources.step2.title: Each card represents one machine
UserGuide.myResources.step2.text: The IP is the machine's connection address; the status in the top-right corner shows whether it's usable. Click the machine name to see its full details.
UserGuide.myResources.step3.title: Use this button to enter the machine
UserGuide.myResources.step3.text: When the machine shows "Running", you can click "Terminal" or "Console" to start working. The three-dot button next to it lets you power on, shut down, or restart.
UserGuide.firewall.title: Firewall
UserGuide.firewall.step1.title: Add a rule to allow a connection
UserGuide.firewall.step1.text: When two machines need to communicate, click "Add Connection" and choose the source, destination, and allowed port. There's no need to add one without a clear requirement.
UserGuide.firewall.step2.title: Lines represent currently allowed connections
UserGuide.firewall.step2.text: Each box represents a VM, and the lines between boxes represent allowed traffic. Click a VM to view its rules; the number on a line is the open port.
UserGuide.firewall.step3.title: These buttons only change how you view it
UserGuide.firewall.step3.text: "Auto-arrange" tidies up positions; "Connection labels" shows or hides ports; "Map" toggles the thumbnail in the bottom-right corner. None of these modify any firewall rules.
UserGuide.reverseProxy.title: Reverse Proxy
UserGuide.reverseProxy.step1.title: Turn a VM service into an easy-to-remember URL
UserGuide.reverseProxy.step1.text: Once the website or API inside your VM is running, click "Add Domain" and choose the VM, the service port, and the URL. The system handles the outbound routing for you.
UserGuide.reverseProxy.step2.title: Each row is one public URL
UserGuide.reverseProxy.step2.text: The VM number is the target machine's ID, and the port is the one the service inside the VM listens on; the HTTPS label indicates a secure connection. Click "Open" to test the URL directly.
UserGuide.domain.title: Domain Management
UserGuide.domain.step1.title: Set up Cloudflare the first time you use this
UserGuide.domain.step1.text: Click "Connection Settings" and enter your Account ID and API Token. "Test Connection" only verifies that the settings are valid — it does not modify DNS.
UserGuide.domain.step2.title: This shows whether the connection is working
UserGuide.domain.step2.text: "Connected" means the platform can manage DNS; the last verified time helps you judge whether the credentials are still valid. Domains can't be loaded while disconnected.
UserGuide.domain.step3.title: The Zones number is how many domains you can manage
UserGuide.domain.step3.text: For example, "Zones (3)" means there are 3 domains available in the account. Click a domain on the left first, and its DNS records will appear on the right.
UserGuide.domain.step4.title: Search or add DNS records here
UserGuide.domain.step4.text: Use the search box to find existing records; "Add Record" creates a mapping between a name and an IP/service. If you're unsure about the record type, don't modify a production domain directly.
UserGuide.aiApi.title: AI API
UserGuide.aiApi.step1.title: These four numbers are your request and key counts
UserGuide.aiApi.step1.text: "Active keys" is the number of keys that can currently call the API; "Expired keys" can no longer be used; "Approved requests" doesn't necessarily equal the number of currently valid keys.
UserGuide.aiApi.step2.title: The four tabs form a complete workflow
UserGuide.aiApi.step2.text: First apply, then once approved go to API Keys to retrieve it, track the review in Request Records, and finally check actual usage in My Usage. Next, we'll walk through each tab in turn.
UserGuide.aiApi.step3.title: Apply: Get eligibility to use the AI API
UserGuide.aiApi.step3.text: This page tells the reviewer "which project needs AI and for how long". You won't get a key immediately after submitting — you'll need to wait for approval.
UserGuide.aiApi.step4.title: The key name is just for your own reference
UserGuide.aiApi.step4.text: We recommend entering your course or project name, such as "Capstone Project Chatbot". It is not the API key itself, and you can change it later.
UserGuide.aiApi.step5.title: The purpose of your request is shown to the reviewer
UserGuide.aiApi.step5.text: Write at least 10 characters, clearly describing the course, project, and the feature you plan to integrate — this is far easier for the reviewer to understand than just writing "test".
UserGuide.aiApi.step6.title: The validity period determines how long the key can be used
UserGuide.aiApi.step6.text: Choose a few days for short-term assignments, or a longer period for long-term projects. Once it expires, the API key stops working, but your request record isn't deleted.
UserGuide.aiApi.step7.title: Submit only once all information is complete
UserGuide.aiApi.step7.text: When the button lights up, your input meets the basic requirements. After submitting, check "Request Records" for progress; once approved, go to "API Keys" to copy your key.
UserGuide.aiApi.step8.title: API Keys: Get the connection info your program needs
UserGuide.aiApi.step8.text: A key only appears on this page after your request is approved. Your program typically needs two values: the Base URL and the API Key. Treat the API Key like a password — don't paste it into assignments or public repositories.
UserGuide.aiApi.step9.title: Each card represents one issued key
UserGuide.aiApi.step9.text: The status shows whether the key can be used, along with its creation and expiration times. If the screen shows "No keys yet", it means no request has been approved yet.
UserGuide.aiApi.step10.title: The difference between show, copy, refresh, and delete
UserGuide.aiApi.step10.text: Copy is for pasting into your own program; Refresh generates a new key and invalidates the old one; Delete can't be undone, and any program currently using that key will fail to connect.
UserGuide.aiApi.step11.title: Request Records: Check where the review stands
UserGuide.aiApi.step11.text: Every AI API request you've submitted is kept on this page. It only shows the request and its review outcome — it's not where you retrieve keys.
UserGuide.aiApi.step12.title: Status and notes tell you what to do next
UserGuide.aiApi.step12.text: "Pending review" means it hasn't been processed yet; once "Approved", go to API Keys to retrieve it; if "Rejected", check the review notes and adjust your request based on the reason given.
UserGuide.aiApi.step13.title: My Usage: See how much AI your program has actually used
UserGuide.aiApi.step13.text: This page shows usage trends and token consumption — it doesn't display or modify your API Key. If usage spikes suddenly, check whether your program is calling the API repeatedly by mistake.
UserGuide.aiApi.step14.title: First choose the date range to analyze
UserGuide.aiApi.step14.text: The 7, 30, and 90-day options only change the report range — they don't limit your key's validity period. The dates on the right show the actual start and end dates currently covered by the report.
UserGuide.aiApi.step15.title: Proxy usage is the consumption from direct AI API calls
UserGuide.aiApi.step15.text: Total calls is the number of requests; Input Tokens is the amount of text sent to the model, and Output Tokens is the amount returned by the model. You can view usage by model further below.
UserGuide.aiApi.step16.title: Template usage is the consumption from the template feature
UserGuide.aiApi.step16.text: This tracks calls made through the AI Template API, counted separately from the direct calls above, so you can tell which type of feature is consuming more.
